register.description: Debug Control Register This register is used by debug software to control all of the basic debug functions.

bitfield.description: Cancel Execution Control Request This bit is used to cancel an execution control request
CPU Reset Request
Ignore DBGM When Halting This bit is used to grant privileges to ignore the DBGM flag when servicing an execution control command that halts code execution
Ignore HPI This bit determines if execution requests issued via DBG_CNTL will honor or ignore HPI state
Enable for External Debug Halt Trigger This bit enables the use of the external debug halt trigger [dbg_halt_req] to support halting the CPU
Enable for External Debug Run Trigger This bit enables the use of the external debug run trigger [dbg_run_req] to support running the CPU
Enable for External Debug Enable This bit enables allows the use of the external debug enable qualifier [dbg_enable] to support debug when coming out of a non-functional state
AET Generated Breakpoint Halt Enable This bit enables halting on the AET imprecise breakpoint debug event
Single Step Type This bit defines the interrupt behavior while single-stepping
Hardware Breakpoint Halt Enable NOTE: Each hardware breakpoint resource also has a local enable
Software Breakpoint Halt Enable This bit enables halting on software breakpoint detection NOTE: If a SWBP opcode is fetched when this enable bit is not set then it is executed as a NOP
Single Step Execution Enable This bit enables single step operation NOTE: See DBG_CNTL:SINGLE_STEP_TYPE for additional information
Execution Mode This bit controls the setting of the execution mode
Global Debug Run Control Load This bit determines if a DBG_CNTL register write can update the HALT field This bit is simply an enable during writes, has no storage, and is always read as zero
Global Debug Run Control This bit controls the global execution state This bit will be read as being set upon entry to HALTED state due to the halted state being entered because of a debug event

register.description: Debug Status Register This register provides all the required system state to the debug tools.

bitfield.description: Ready Status Continuously Inactive [sticky] This bit indicates the ready status of the CPU and is used to detect a CPU hang condition It is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set

External Run Trigger Status This bit indicates that a qualified external run trigger was detected since the last time it was cleared It is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set

External Halt Trigger Status This bit indicates that a qualified external halt trigger was detected since the last time it was cleared It is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set
External Debug Enable Qualifier Status This bit indicates the state of the external debug enable qualifier
State of the Interrupt During Suspend CPU State This bit indicates that an interrupt during suspend [IDS] is being serviced by the CPU

CPU Reset Occurred [sticky] This bit is used to determine if the CPU reset has been active at least one clock since the last time it was cleared This is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set NOTE: This register has no reset value, instead it is affected by the occurrence of a CPU reset
CPU Reset Status This bit indicates the reset state of the CPU core

CPU Clocks Active [sticky] This is a sticky bit which is set when a rising edge is seen on the CPUs functional clock This is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set
CPU is IDLE This bit indicates the idle state of the CPU core

State of Non-Invasive Permissions This bit indicates whether the next execute packet has Non-Invasive Permissions It is used to detect that the CPU is executing code that is not allotted Non-Invasive Debug Permissions
State of Invasive Permissions This bit indicates whether the next execute packet has Invasive Permissions It is used to detect that the CPU is executing secure code and can not be debugged
State of the HPI Privilege Window This bit indicates that a high priority interrupt has been taken but has not yet been completed
State of the DBGM Privilege Window This bit reflects the state of the DBGM privilege window
Execution Halted within an Interrupt During Suspend [IDS] This bit indicates that the CPU has halted while executing an IDS
Execution Halted Due to an AET generated breakpoint This bit indicates that an AET-generated breakpoint has halted code execution
Execution Halted Due to an external debug halt request
Execution Halted Due to a application update of the HALT bit
Execution Halted Due to a Single Step This bit indicates that the halt occurred due to the completion of a single step operation
Execution Halted Due to CPU Reset or a halt request made during CPU Reset
Execution Halted Due to a Hardware Breakpoint This bit indicates that the halt occurred due to the detection of a hardware breakpoint
Execution Halted Due to a SWBP This bit indicates that the halt occurred due to a software breakpoint being detected

Indirect Access Port Request Canceled This bit indicates that an IAP read or write request has been canceled [eg due to Port Reset, CPU Reset, New debug context] since the last time it was cleared It is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set

Debug Command Request Canceled This bit indicates that a debug request has been canceled [by a NEW_HALT or by DBG_CNTL:CANCEL_EXE while a previously issued command was pending] since the last time it was cleared It is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set

Execution Restart This bit indicates that the core execution resumed due to a debug command since the last time it was cleared It is a sticky bit A simultaneous set and clear condition causes the bit to be set
Execution State This bit indicates the execution status of the CPU
Debug Context Status This bit indicates that the processor has halted at a new location [or debug context] relative to the previously active debug location

register.description: Ownership Control and Status Register

bitfield.description: The Ownership State

This bit is used to obtain exclusive ownership of the debug module for either the debug initiator or the application initiator Reads will always return 0 If the current state is NOT_OWNED o A debugger-initiated write of 1 will claim the module for use by the debugger initiator o An application-initiated write of 1 will claim the module for use by the application initiator If the current state is DBG_OWNED o A debugger-initiated write of 0 will release ownership o A debugger-initiated write of 1 has no effect o Application writes have no effect If the current state is APP_OWNED o An application-initiated write of 0 will release ownership o A debugger-initiated write of 0 will release ownership o A write of 1 has not effect

register.description: Indirect Memory Control and Status Register This register is used to control the behavior of the indirect memory controller.

bitfield.description: Port Reset
Indicates the access code returned for the last read transaction

Indicates the bus error code returned for a transaction This field indicates the memory access error code returned by the subsystem interconnect The first non-zero error is captured and held until it is cleared by a port reset

Indicates the bus status [ready state] of the processor interface selected by MEM_PAGE This bit indicates the current availability state [the bus ready value] for the interface selected by MEM_PAGE It is used by the debug agent to determine if the interface is in a hung state

Indicates the state of the access port This field indicates that the settings of the indirect access port [control, context, data, or address] registers have changed before a previous access completed Once it is set to 1 it stays asserted until it is cleared by a port reset
Pending Memory Request Completed This bit indicates the status of the memory port

Post Mortem Qualification This bit controls if a memory access is submitted as part of a postmortem analysis acitivty This bit will be set only when normal debug initiated accesses are no longer possible due to a system crash When set, the CPU will service an indirect access port request independent of all other memory qualifiers or normally required architectural state dependencies
VMID Qualification This bit controls if a VMID context match is required of accesses submitted by the indirect controller The VMID reference is programmed using DBG_INDRCT_CTXT2

Processor State Qualification Enable This bit controls if a processor state match is required of accesses submitted by the indirect controller The processor states of interest are programmed using DBG_INDRCT_CTXT2

Debug Context Qualification Enable This bit controls if a DCTXT context match is required of accesses submitted by the indirect controller The DCTXT reference and mask are programmed using DBG_INDRCT_CTXT0 and DBG_INDRCT_CTXT1
Access size of the next transaction

Page designator for the next access This bit defines the page index of the memory page targeted for subsequent transactions The parameters of the pages supported in the system are available in the DBG_INDRCT_CAP register
Ignore Context This bit determines whether memory/register accesses through the indirect controller will honor or ignore IDS and debug context changes
Ignore DBGM When Halting This bit is used to grant privileges to ignore the DBGM flag when servicing a request to access memory or registers via the Indirect Access Port

Auto increment address on each access This bit determines if the address used for the memory access auto-increments For read transactions, the auto-increment occurs when the previous value is read from the data registers This will automatically launch another read transaction from the new address For write transactions, the auto-increment occurs when the write completes A new write is not launched until new data is written into the data registers The auto-increment feature is disabled on any error [the bit stays set] and is not re-enabled until the error is cleared
R/W Control for next accesses This bit determines if the port is executing read or write operations

register.description: Indirect Memory Context ID Register 0 This register is used to designate the desired debug context of accesses initiated via the indirect access port mechanism. Context ID Register 0 holds the reference value for the CPU register DBGCTXT. When enabled (via DBG_INDRCT_CNTL::MEM_QUAL_DCTXT ) this register is used in conjunction with DBG_INDRCT_CTXT1 and the state of the CPU register DBGCTXT to determine if the debug context criteria for an indirect access port access is met.

bitfield.description: This field is used to define the context qualification mask associated with DBG_INDRCT_CTXT0 An asserted bit means the corresponding DBGCTXT_REF bit is compared

register.description: Indirect Memory Context ID Register 1 This register is used to designate the desired debug context of accesses initiated via the indirect access port mechanism. Context ID Register 1 holds the MASK value for DBG_INDRCT_CTXT0.

bitfield.description: When used, this field is initialized with the DBGCTXT reference value

register.description: Indirect Memory Context ID Register 2 This register is used to designate the desired debug context of accesses initiated via the indirect access port mechanism. Context ID Register 2 holds the context criteria for processor operating modes and the VMID. When enabled (via DBG_INDRCT_CNTL::MEM_QUAL_PROC and DBG_INDRCT_CNTL::MEM_QUAL_VMID) this register is used, in conjunction with current CPU state and VMID settings, to determine if the debug context criteria for an indirect access port access is met.

bitfield.description: Processor Mode Reference When enabled, this bit-field controls which processor modes the associated hardware breakpoint is active for -----0 : Inactive during Non-Root User -----1 : Active during Non-Root User ----0- : Inactive during Non-Root Supervisor ----1- : Active during Non-Root Supervisor ---0-- : Inactive during Root User ---1-- : Active during Root User --0--- : Inactive during Root Supervisor --1--- : Active during Root Supervisor -0---- : Inactive during Secure User -1---- : Active during Secure User 0----- : Inactive during Secure Supervisor 1----- : Active during Secure Supervisor
When used, this field is initialized with the VMID reference

register.description: Indirect Memory Address Register 0

bitfield.description: Low order address bits for designating the target of an indirect debug access This bit field holds the 32 LSBs of the address of an indirect debug port transaction If the port is set for auto-incrementing addresses [DBG_INDRCT_CNTL:MEM_INC_ADDR = 1], this field will be incremented by the access size each time a transaction completes

register.description: Indirect Memory Address Register 1

bitfield.description: High order address bits for designating the target of an indirect debug access This bit field holds the 32 MSBs of the address of an indirect debug port transaction If the port is set for auto-incrementing addresses [DBG_INDRCT_CNTL:MEM_INC_ADDR = 1], this field will be incremented by one when the DBG_INDRCT_ADDR0 rolls over

register.description: Indirect Memory Data Register 0 Data is packed using little endian byte numbering

bitfield.description: Data bits of the read or write transaction This bit field holds bits 31:00 of the data of an indirect debug port transaction If Writing data: This register must be written after the address registers If Reading data This register will have valid read data when the transaction is complete [MEM_PORT_STAT == 10b]

register.description: Indirect Memory Data Register 1 Data is packed using little endian byte numbering

bitfield.description: Data bits of the read or write transaction This bit field holds bits 63:32 of the data of an indirect debug port transaction If Writing data: This register must be written after the address registers If Reading data This register will have valid read data when the transaction is complete [MEM_PORT_STAT == 10b]
